title: The Ultimate Flex (Raising the Dead)
paragraphs: §The Death of Lazarus

A man was sick—Lazarus of Bethany, the town of Mary and her sister Martha. This was the same Mary who massaged the Lord's feet with fragrant oils and then wiped them with her hair. It was her brother Lazarus who was sick. So the sisters sent word to Jesus: "Master, the one you love so much is sick."
When Jesus got the message, he said, "This sickness won't end in death. It will become a chance to show God's glory by glorifying God's Son."

Jesus loved Martha and her sister and Lazarus. But oddly, when he heard Lazarus was sick, he stayed where he was for two more days. After the two days, he said to his disciples, "Let's go back to Judea."
They said, "Rabbi, you can't do that. The Jews are out to kill you, and you're going back?"

Jesus replied, "Aren't there twelve hours of daylight? Anyone who walks in daylight doesn't stumble, because there's plenty of light from the sun. Walking at night, he might well stumble, because he can't see where he's going."
He said these things, and then announced, "Our friend Lazarus has fallen asleep. I'm going to wake him up."
The disciples said, "Master, if he's asleep, he'll get good rest and wake up fine." Jesus was talking about death, while his disciples thought he meant taking a nap.
Then Jesus was blunt: "Lazarus died. And I'm glad for your sakes that I wasn't there. You're about to get new reasons to believe. Now let's go to him."
That's when Thomas, the one called the Twin, said to his companions, "Come on. We might as well die with him."

When Jesus finally got there, he found Lazarus already four days dead. Bethany was near Jerusalem, only a couple of miles away, and many of the Jews were visiting Martha and Mary, sympathizing with them over their brother. Martha heard Jesus was coming and went out to meet him. Mary stayed in the house.
Martha said, "Master, if you'd been here, my brother wouldn't have died. Even now, I know that whatever you ask God, he will give you."
Jesus said, "Your brother will rise again."
Martha replied, "I know he'll rise again in the resurrection at the end of time."

"You don't have to wait for the End. I am, right now, Resurrection and Life. The one who believes in me, even though he dies, will live. And everyone who lives believing in me doesn't ultimately die at all. Do you believe this?"
"Yes, Master. All along I've believed you are the Messiah, the Son of God who comes into the world."
After saying this, she went to her sister Mary and whispered in her ear, "The Teacher is here and is asking for you."

The moment she heard that, she jumped up and ran out to him. Jesus hadn't yet entered the town but was still at the place where Martha had met him. When her sympathizing Jewish friends saw Mary run off, they followed, thinking she was heading to the tomb to weep there. Mary came to where Jesus was waiting and fell at his feet, saying, "Master, if only you'd been here, my brother wouldn't have died."
When Jesus saw her sobbing, and the Jews with her sobbing, a deep anger welled up inside him. He said, "Where did you put him?"
"Master, come and see," they said. Now Jesus wept.
The Jews said, "Look how deeply he loved him."
Others among them said, "Well, if he loved him so much, why didn't he do something to keep him from dying? After all, he opened the eyes of a blind man."

Then Jesus, anger welling up inside him again, arrived at the tomb. It was a simple cave in the hillside with a slab of stone laid against it. Jesus said, "Remove the stone." Martha, the dead man's sister, said, "Master, by now there's a stench. He's been dead four days!"
Jesus looked her in the eye. "Didn't I tell you that if you believed, you would see the glory of God?"

Then, to the others: "Go ahead, take away the stone." They removed the stone. Jesus raised his eyes to heaven and prayed, "Father, I'm grateful that you've listened to me. I know you always listen, but because of this crowd standing here I've said this out loud, so they might believe you sent me."
Then he shouted, "Lazarus, come out!" And he came out—a dead man, wrapped from head to toe, with a cloth over his face. Jesus told them, "Unwrap him and let him loose."
§The Man Who Creates God-Signs

That was a turning point for many of the Jews who were with Mary. They saw what Jesus did and believed in him. But some went back to the Pharisees and reported on Jesus. The high priests and Pharisees called a meeting of the Jewish ruling body. "What do we do now?" they asked. "This man keeps doing things, creating God-signs. If we let him go on, pretty soon everyone will believe in him, and the Romans will come and take away what little power and privilege we still have."

Then one of them—Caiaphas, the designated Chief Priest that year—spoke up: "Don't you know anything? Can't you see it's to our advantage that one man dies for the people rather than the whole nation being destroyed?" He didn't say this on his own; as Chief Priest that year he unknowingly prophesied that Jesus was about to die as a sacrifice for the nation—and not only for the nation, but so that all God's scattered, exiled children might be gathered into one people.

From that day on, they plotted to kill him. So Jesus no longer went out in public among the Jews. He withdrew into the countryside bordering the desert, to a town called Ephraim, and stayed there quietly with his disciples.

The Jewish Passover was coming up. Crowds were making their way from the countryside up to Jerusalem to get ready for the Feast. They were curious about Jesus. There was a lot of talk about him among those standing around in the Temple: "What do you think? Will he show up at the Feast or not?"
Meanwhile, the high priests and Pharisees had given orders that anyone who knew where he was should report it. They were all set to arrest him.
